title: Do not persist stale Meridian tab IDs after normalization failure
description:
background.js normalizeMeridianTab catches a rejected chrome.tabs.update call but then continues to move and remember the original tab object. When the update failed because the tab/window disappeared, this persists a known-stale managed tab ID and returns apparent success.

Change normalization to return a failure sentinel (prefer null) immediately after the update rejects, skip move/remember, and make callers tolerate that result. Preserve benign tab/window teardown handling without masking unrelated programming failures where practical. Mirror the change in meridian-extension/background.js.

Update lifecycle tests so a disappeared tab is not remembered, and rerun the per-window ensure, restoration, navigation handoff, second-window deduplication, and full packaged-parity suite.
label: Bug

activity.content:
Implemented the stale Meridian tab normalization fix.

- `normalizeMeridianTab` now returns `null` immediately when `chrome.tabs.update` rejects, preventing any subsequent move or persistence of the stale tab.
- Mirrored the worker change in `meridian-extension/background.js`.
- Updated lifecycle regression coverage to assert the vanished tab is neither moved nor remembered and that normalization reports `null`.
- Existing ensure, focus, and event callers already tolerate the null sentinel.

Verification:
- Targeted lifecycle scenarios (restoration, per-window ensure, navigation handoff, replacement/deduplication): 4/4 passed.
- Packaged runtime parity: 1/1 passed.
- Full test suite: 156/156 passed.
- Syntax checks for both background workers passed.
- Diff whitespace check passed.

Reviewer follow-up applied: normalizeMeridianTab now also returns null when chrome.tabs.move rejects, so a tab that disappears after update but before move is not remembered as managed. Mirrored in meridian-extension/background.js and added a regression asserting the move failure returns null and leaves the remembered list empty. Validation: targeted lifecycle suite 15/15; full suite 156/156; both workers pass node --check; source/package parity and code diff checks pass.
